To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in patients with internal carotid occlusions, the number of collateral pathways and cerebral vasomotor response are important predictors of the outcome.

in patients with symptomatic and asymptomatic internal carid artery occlusion, the outcome is related to the number of intracranial anatomic collateral pathways and to the cerebral vasomotor response to apnea.

the number and patency of collateral pathways and the degree of cerebral vasomotor response to hyperventilation are independent predictors of ipsilateral stroke risk in patients with caroid occlusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cerebral hemodynamics in patients with carotic artery occlusion.
the role played by collateral circulation and VMR in determining outcome after carotid occlusions.
the role of the cerebral hemodynamic status on the risk of ipsi-lateral ischemic stroke in patients with internal carotid occlusions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of ischemic events occurring in patients with car otid occlusive disease depends on a complex interaction between the number of collateral pathways and the VMR.

the presence of collateral pathways is associated with a better outcome and the absence of collateral pathways is not a good prognostic sign, whereas the number of collateral pathways is related to the degree of hemodynamic impairment.
a normal VMR is the best predictor of a favorable outcome, and an impaired VMR the best predictor of an unfavorable outcome, in patients with caroid artery occlusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of collateral pathways and the cerebral vasomotor reserve (BHI) are important factors to predict stroke recurrence in carotid occluded patients.
the number of collateral pathways and the BHI are the main determinants of the risk of stroke in patients who have internal carotid occlusions.
in the presence of carotid occlusions, the risk of stroke is related to the degree of collateral circulation and cerebral vasomotor reserve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of stroke in patients affected by internal carotid occlusions depends on both the anatomic and functional status of intracranial collaterals.
patients with carotids occlusion and no collateral vessels are at high risk of ipsilateral cerebrovascular events, even if they are asymptomatic.

the presence of intracranial collaterals is not sufficient to protect against ischemic events in patients with internal carotid occlusions; the collateral status must be considered in the context of the patient’s overall cerebrovascular reactivity.
